items.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]
items.q: "my aunt, that Marjorie knows of course, was very helpful to me"

ctx.x: Were you a fan of the big bands during the 40’s?

Oh yes, yes indeed. The first real big band that impressed me that I knew anything about was Casa Loma. I had an orchestra in The Pines Hotel in Digby, Nova Scotia, which is CPR Hotel in 1931, my third year in medical school. And one of the interesting things about that, I don’t know whether it should be publicized or not, but my aunt, that Marjorie knows of course, was very helpful to me in everything I did. She gave me my first blood pressure machine when I was a medical student. She also was around St. Stephen…

to another passenger to take it off and carry with the suitcase so they’d have no trouble with customs. But he was a great musician. And he was the one who said “have you fellas ever heard of the Casa Loma orchestra?” And we hadn’t and he just was so enthralled, and he said “you should hear them.” And then that was my first big band.
